sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
மாருதி மனங்குளிர்ந்து அருள்வாய் ஆனந்த
வாரிதி உன் பதகமல சேவையெனும் மாநிதி
sections.translit:
mAruthi manangkuLirndhu aruLvAy Anandha
vArithi un padhakamala sEvaiyenum mAnidhi
sections.en: May happiness rain down upon us, Oh Lord, from your cool and compassionate heart. Bestow upon us the greatest treasure: devout service at your sacred feet.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
சாரதி நேயனே உன் சஹஸ்ரநாமமே என்
ஆரதி ஆழியைக் கடந்தது போல் அதிவேகமாய் வந்து
sections.translit:
sArathi nEyanE un sahasranAmamE en
Arathi Azhiyaik kadandhadhu pOl adhivEgamAy vandhu
sections.en: You are the friend of the One who steers the soul through the battlefield of life. Chanting your thousand divine names is my ritual act to dispel darkness and receive light. Please rush here with the same swiftness with which you crossed the ocean, and grace us with your presence.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
ஊரினை அழித்தே போரினைத் தொடங்கினாய்
வேரினை பறித்திட வெற்பினை ஏந்தினாய்
மாரினை பிளந்தே மாதவ பக்தியைக் காட்டினாய்
பாரினை ராமநாம ப்ரவாஹத்தில் ஆழ்த்திய
sections.translit:
Urinai azhitthE pOrinaith thodanginAy
vErinai paRitthida veRpinai EndhinAy
mArinai piLandhE mAdhava bakthiyaik kAttinAy
pArinai rAmanAma pravAhatthil Azhtthiya
sections.en: You destroyed a city and ignited a war. You carried an entire mountain to retrieve a handful of life-saving herbs. You tore open your chest to reveal and proclaim your unwavering devotion to Lord Rama, the Supreme Vishnu. In boundless compassion, you soaked the earth in the unbroken stream of the divine name of Rama.

notes: The anupallavi word Sarathi here denotes the Supreme who guides or chariots us through the battleground of life on earth. The charanam of the song has references to familiar acts of Anchaneya from the epic Ramayana (and Krittivasi Ramayana). For details of Lines 1 and 2 of the charanam, see: ஶ்ரீமத் வால்மீகி ராமாயண ஸாரம், உரை ஆசிரியர் அண்ணா, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை – 4, ஸூந்தர காண்டம், லங்கா தகனம், பக்கம் 628 – 645; யுத்த காண்டம், இந்திரஜித்து வதம், பக்கம் 755 – 758. The scene in which Hanuman tears open his chest is not found in the original Valmiki Ramayana. Instead, it appears in later retellings of the Ramayana that amplify certain devotional ideas, such as the Krittivasi Ramayana authored by the 15th-century Bengali poet Krittibas Ojha (1381–1461). After Rama’s coronation, he distributed gifts to those present. He presented a beautiful pearl necklace to Sita and suggested that she give it to the person she loved and admired the most. Sita passed the necklace to Hanuman. Hanuman gladly accepted it, but then threw it to the ground, picked up each pearl, and began chewing them. The audience, including Lakshmana, was appalled by this strange behavior. Lakshmana mockingly asked Hanuman what he was searching for in the pearls. Hanuman replied that he did not value anything that did not bear Rama’s name. Lakshmana then teased him about his own continued existence despite Rama’s name not being visibly inscribed on his body. Immediately, Hanuman tore open his chest, and everyone was astonished to see Rama’s name engraved on all his bones. This episode illustrates Hanuman’s extreme devotion. In some folkloric versions, the audience sees images of Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana, within Hanuman’s chest. See more details below: Hanuman tears open chest in an act of devotion Krittivasi Ramayana narrates Hanuman tearing open his chest Krittivasi verses and meaning: তখন হনুমান কহে বিনয় বচন। “নাথ, কিসে করিব আমি তোমার প্রমাণ?”॥ দেখিতে দেখিতে হনুমান বক্ষ বিদারিল। রাম লক্ষ্মণ সীতা হৃদয়ে দেখাইল॥ দেখি রামচন্দ্র কাঁদেন করুণা সহিত।লক্ষ্মণ মূর্ছিত হনু বক্ষ দেখিয়া অতীত॥ সীতা দেবী কহে কাঁপিয়া বাণী। “এহেন ভকতি কেহ না করিবে জানি॥” Translation: Then Hanuman spoke words of humility: “O Lord, by what means shall I give proof of my devotion?” Before everyone’s eyes, Hanuman tore open his chest and revealed Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita dwelling within his heart. Seeing this, Rama wept, overcome with emotion; Lakshmana fainted upon beholding Hanuman’s opened breast. And Lady Sita spoke, her voice trembling: “Such devotion as this, I know, that no one else can ever show.”
